subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which is the SI unit of speed?
questions.explain: Speed is distance travelled per unit time, so its SI unit is metres per second (m/s).

questions.q: On a distance–time graph, what does the gradient (slope) of the line represent?
questions.explain: Gradient equals change in distance divided by change in time, which is the speed.

questions.q: On a speed–time graph, what does the area under the line represent?
questions.explain: The area under a speed–time graph gives distance because it multiplies speed by time.

questions.q: A car travels 100 m in 20 s at constant speed. What is its average speed?
questions.explain: Speed = distance ÷ time = 100 ÷ 20 = 5 m/s.

questions.q: Which equation correctly gives the weight W of an object?
questions.explain: Weight is the gravitational force on a mass, W = mg, where g is the gravitational field strength.

questions.q: Which statement about mass and weight is correct?
options: Mass is the amount of matter in a body and stays the same everywhere; weight is the gravitational force on it and can vary
Mass and weight are the same quantity measured in different units
Weight stays the same everywhere but mass changes with location
Mass is measured in newtons and weight in kilograms
questions.explain: Mass (kg) is constant, while weight (N) depends on the gravitational field strength at the location.

questions.q: Which equation defines density?
questions.explain: Density is mass per unit volume, ρ = m/V.

questions.q: An object has a mass of 500 g and a volume of 250 cm³. What is its density?
questions.explain: Density = mass ÷ volume = 500 ÷ 250 = 2 g/cm³.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explain: Force is measured in newtons (N), where 1 N accelerates 1 kg at 1 m/s².

questions.q: A moving object experiences a resultant force of zero. What happens to its motion?
options: It continues to move at constant velocity
questions.explain: With no resultant force there is no acceleration, so the object keeps a constant velocity.

questions.q: Which equation gives the momentum p of an object?
questions.explain: Momentum is mass multiplied by velocity, p = mv, measured in kg m/s.

questions.q: A resultant force accelerates a 4 kg mass at 3 m/s². What is the size of the force?
questions.explain: Using F = ma, F = 4 × 3 = 12 N.

questions.q: How is the work done by a force calculated?
options: force × distance moved in the direction of the force
questions.explain: Work done W = F × d, the force multiplied by distance moved in its direction, measured in joules.

questions.q: Which statement best describes power?
options: The rate at which work is done or energy is transferred
The total energy stored in a body
The force acting per unit area
The product of energy and time
questions.explain: Power is energy transferred (or work done) per unit time, P = E/t.

questions.q: As an object falls freely towards the ground, which energy transfer occurs?
options: Gravitational potential energy to kinetic energy
Kinetic energy to gravitational potential energy
Kinetic energy to thermal energy only
questions.explain: As height decreases the store of gravitational potential energy is transferred to kinetic energy, so the object speeds up.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.explain: Power is measured in watts (W), where 1 W = 1 joule per second.

questions.q: Which equation defines pressure?
questions.explain: Pressure is the force acting normally per unit area, p = F/A.

questions.q: How does the pressure within a liquid change?
options: It increases with depth and with the density of the liquid
It depends only on the shape of the container
It is the same at every depth
questions.explain: Pressure in a liquid is given by p = ρgh, so it rises with both depth and density.

questions.q: The SI unit of pressure, the pascal (Pa), is equivalent to which of the following?
questions.explain: Since pressure = force ÷ area, one pascal equals one newton per square metre.

questions.q: A force of 200 N acts normally on a surface of area 4 m². What is the pressure?
questions.explain: Pressure = force ÷ area = 200 ÷ 4 = 50 Pa.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Physics (0625) syllabus; Motion, Forces & Energy
